newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Nov. 25, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Microsoft Corp announced plans at Comdex to release a native code compiler for Sun Microsystems Inc's Java language that would let software developers create Java-executable programs, but that run only in Windows, PC Week reported Nov. 25.

International Business Machines Corp plans to ship in first quarter of 1997 its first notebook network computer, dubbed the Think Client. IBM's device functions like a desktop NC equivalent, retrieving Java-based data from a server through a Windows 95 or an OS/2 interface and it will have a small hard drive and minimal memory, PC Week reported Nov. 25.

COMPUTERWORLD - Personal computers cost too much to maintain and do not deliver enough return on investment, said many computer companies and big users at the Comdex computer trade show last week, Computerworld reported Nov. 25.

Information systems managers at major corporations are trying to turn their World Wide Web sites into the cyber-equivalent of Alice's Restaurant - a place where you can get anything you want, Computerworld reported Nov. 25.

COMMUNICATIONS WEEK - Cisco Systems Inc is preparing to introduce this spring high-capacity network routers capable of transmitting up to 80 gigabits, or billions of bits, of data a second -- the capacity required to handle the heavy traffic of telecommunications carriers and Internet Service Providers, Communications Week reported in its November 25 issue.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Intel Corp's upcoming Klamath processor will not be any faster than its existing 200 megahertz PentiumPro chip, said several original equipment manufacturers working with the new chip, CRN reported Nov. 25. The chip is expected to be unveiled in April with a speed of 233 megahertz but OEMs said they did not see these gains.
International Business Machines Corp proposed a broad-based super alliance with Microsoft Corp focusing on network operating systems, clustering technology and services, CRN reported Nov. 25.

INFOWORLD - Intel Corp plans to formally announce its so-called P55C processor with multimedia capabilities for desktop and notebook computers on January 8, 1997, Infoworld reported Nov. 25. PC vendors plan simultaneous rollouts of systems based on the new chip.

A growing rebellion among system suppliers could lead to higher support costs as hardware vendors cease distributing the Microsoft Windows NT operating system, with Compaq Computer Corp, Hewlett-Packard Co, IBM Corp and Digital Equipment Corp not bundling NT with their hardware, Infoworld reported Nov. 25.

INFORMATION WEEK - Informix Corp will unveil next week at DB/Expo in New York its highly anticipated Universal Server software, an object-oriented relational database that stores video, voice, sound and other data types, Information Week reported Nov. 25. But some competitors and customers say Informix's strategy is flawed and that important pieces are still missing, making performance impossible to measure.

Compaq Computer Corp is establishing a systems integration program and testing a build-to-order strategy for its PCs as part of an effort to transform itself into an entreprise computing powerhouse of the 21st century, Information Week reported Nov. 25.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - Pioneers of digital video (or digital versatile) disk technology are poised to begin shipping in next year's first and second quarters, believing that the technology will take off as some of the critical issues such as copyright protection, are resolved, EBN reported Nov. 25.

VLSI Technology Inc, which said last week it will shut down its fab in San Jose, Calif., is the latest among semiconductor companies deciding to scale back manufacturing operations or give them up entirely, as they are weakened by falling prices, slack demand, and uncertain markets, EBN reported Nov. 25.

ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING TIMES - Intel Corp is pushing efforts that may slice more than $500 off the original equipment manufacturer cost of a multimedia PC with software solutions in place of costly chip sets for the new Talisman graphics architecture and DVD, EE Times reported Nov. 25.

Waging a "war for the eyeballs," the PC will push deeper into TV territory next year, propelled by new software from Microsoft Corp and a number of new combo PC/TV systems, with many of the top five PC makers expected to launch hybrid systems next year, EE Times reported Nov. 25.

MACWEEK - As Apple Computer Inc continues to redraw its operating system landscape, two top AppleSoft executives, Ike Nassi, senior vice president and Mitch Allen, vice president in charge of MacOS engineering, resigned this month, MacWeek reported Nov. 25.
